title: Management: a dashboard Claude keeps up to date
summary: The management session of our 17 November 2026 webinar: a territory dashboard in Claude, tasks that come back every week, and where the data lives.
body_markdown:
In the last session of our[17 November webinar](https://www.leadbay.ai/blog/ai-agents-sales-marketing-webinar) (in French), Ludovic Granger shows what replaces the CRM’s static view for him: interfaces he calls « génératives » (generative), which follow the week’s plan, with the CRM kept up to date underneath.


## 1. Dashboards and tasks that come back


[Watch at 41:17](https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=H0wl_2B_mE4&t=2477s) . In Claude, his dashboards are artifacts he opens again every week, next to his recurring tasks. The method: write the prompt yourself, judge the result, then make it a task that comes back every week: « l’IA va le faire pour vous » (the AI will do it for you).


In the guide:[4.7 Set the routines for prospecting, sales and marketing](https://www.leadbay.ai/guides#guide-4-7) .


## 2. The manager’s dashboard


[Watch at 42:16](https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=H0wl_2B_mE4&t=2536s) . His territory, France, split between two reps, north and south. He follows his 90-day plan, the week’s meetings, the prospecting actions and the conversion rate. The numbers shown during the webinar are demo data.


The dashboard is connected to the team’s email, phones and CRM: Ludovic sees what happens live, and steps in by email or phone when a prospect doesn’t answer. Every morning, a list tells each rep who to call and what to say; the answer they note updates the CRM: « Zoé se réveille tous les matins et elle sait exactement ce qu’elle doit faire » (Zoé wakes up every morning and knows exactly what to do). The dashboard also suggests the week’s decisions.


In the guide:[2.12 Split the market between your reps](https://www.leadbay.ai/guides#guide-2-12) ,[2.11 Prepare today’s calls and follow-ups](https://www.leadbay.ai/guides#guide-2-11) ,[4.2 Track the impact of your sales and marketing](https://www.leadbay.ai/guides#guide-4-2) ,[4.3 Review the pipeline with your team](https://www.leadbay.ai/guides#guide-4-3) .


## 3. Where the data lives


[Watch at 49:59](https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=H0wl_2B_mE4&t=2999s) and[at 53:36](https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=H0wl_2B_mE4&t=3216s) . Ludovic separates three things: data, qualification and workflow. Leadbay brings the market’s data and its qualification. The workflow happens in your AI, which knows your company and is connected to your tools.


Your internal data (spreadsheets, CRM, ERP) connects beside it. Leadbay did it with Supabase, a database where the data is stored and secured and which the AI queries; large groups do it in their data lakes, on Azure, Snowflake or Databricks. His image: « c’est un peu votre Google Drive de votre IA » (it’s a bit like your AI’s Google Drive).
